description: Illustrative public package containing meteorological predictors, static OGS descriptors, physics-generated weak labels, and processed measurement-derived reference labels.
The package demonstrates the data schema and alignment interface; it is not a release of the complete raw measurement archive or proprietary station records.

The reference labels are processed, measurement-derived records supplied by a third-party data provider. The authors did not conduct the original field measurements or receive the raw optical signals.
Four seven-day periods in 2025: Jan 1-7, Apr 1-7, Jul 1-7, and Oct 1-7; five-minute processed-record grid; 8,064 records per station; 80,640 station-time records in total.

The compact example contains one meteorological record per station-valid_time and rotates lead_min over the valid-time grid. It demonstrates the input schema rather than a complete operational issue-time by lead-time forecast cube.
Weak labels are generated from meteorological predictors and station metadata. The detailed internal surface-layer parameterization is not released in this public example.
All retained weak-label samples receive equal weight during pretraining. No sample-level confidence weight is used.

Only the class commercial_optical_turbulence_scintillometer is disclosed. Exact models, serial identifiers, site-specific configurations, calibration records, and photographs are withheld under the data provider's disclosure restrictions.
The nominal reference height is h0 = 100 m. It is not the horizontal optical-path length or the simulated receiver-aperture height.

The authors use the quality flag supplied with the processed records. Only valid reference targets enter fine-tuning and evaluation; no additional author-defined statistical outlier threshold is applied.
Missing or non-valid reference targets are not interpolated, imputed, forward-filled, or generated from neighboring samples.

Join region descriptors by station; join weather and weak labels by station + valid_time_UTC; join weather and reference labels by station after matching timestamp_UTC to valid_time_UTC; retain lead_min from the weather table.
